title: Reader equations
description: What the Reader writes to runs/<paper-slug>/equations.json. The Verifier does not edit this file.

source.description: Path or label of the PDF or LaTeX the equations were lifted from.

number.description: Equation number as printed in the paper.

line.description: 1-based source line of the displayed equation.

sympy.description: Optional machine form of the equation, written by the Reader, read by the Verifier. Strings use SymPy syntax: ** for powers, explicit * for products. Every name must be declared in symbols or functions, apart from standard SymPy functions and constants (sqrt, exp, sin, pi, I, ...).

relation.description: How lhs relates to rhs. Defaults to equality. approx: \approx or \simeq (lhs/rhs -> 1 in the regime, or the error is of the stated order, or within the stated tolerance). sim: \sim (same order: lhs/rhs stays finite and nonzero in the regime; the O(1) factor is not checked). approx and sim need a regime.

regime.description: Where an approximate relation is meant to hold, as stated in the paper. If the paper states none, give only a note saying so; the Verifier then reports UNCHECKED instead of guessing.

symbol.description: Declared symbol that goes to the limit, e.g. a small parameter eps.

order.description: Size of the neglected terms in SymPy syntax, e.g. "eps**2" for an error O(eps**2).

tolerance.description: Relative tolerance, when the paper quotes a numerical approximation (e.g. 0.01 for 1%).

note.description: The paper's wording of the regime, e.g. "for k H >> 1".

symbols.description: Every symbol in lhs and rhs, with the SymPy assumptions the paper states or implies.

functions.description: Names used as undefined functions, e.g. x for x(t).
